## 3. Household Roles (continued)

| Design question | Japan | Korea | Thailand | Gulf |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Staff mode** | N/A — live-in domestic staff are rare; omit from the Japan SKU | Rare; omit at launch, revisit for the premium villa segment | Lightweight version: Bangkok upper-middle homes increasingly employ helpers — service-area controls only, no purchases, no family data | **P0:** distinct role with employer-scoped permissions — climate/lighting in service areas, no cameras, no locks, no purchases, no access to family history; **staff-language ASR** (Tagalog, Hindi/Urdu, Bahasa Indonesia, Amharic); time-bounded schedules tied to work hours; staff enrolled for *recognition*, never for privileged authentication |

**3.1 Role mechanics (global).** Voice profiles enroll at setup; voice-match gates purchases, locks, cameras, and messaging. Guest access auto-expires (default 24 hours). Child → Adult transitions at a parent-configurable age. Role-priority arbitration is configuration, not law: the assistant defers, it never adjudicates family politics aloud — a device that publicly rules "Dad outranks Grandma" has failed in all four markets.

## 4. Privacy Signaling

In these markets, privacy is not a policy page — it is a **visible, physical, continuously broadcast posture**. The device must look trustworthy to a guest who has never read a word of the terms of service.

**4.1 Universal signals (Layer 1, identical everywhere):**

- Physical mic disconnect with a tactile switch position; hardwired LED that software cannot override; camera shutters that visibly close.
